rule: accumulated MIXED Track-B channels, ranked by |alone-AUC - .5| on FIT+MINE only
selected_parents: Reads as freshly minted rather than a circulated chestnut
Cleanliness of commitment to one delivery format

candidates.criterion: Reads as freshly minted rather than a circulated chestnut
candidates.instruction: Score how much the item reads as a joke the writer constructed versus a standard that has been in circulation for decades and is reproduced here verbatim. 10 = the premise, the pivot and the phrasing all feel newly assembled; a well-read judge does not recognise it. 5 = a familiar frame with a new payload, or a new frame with a familiar payload. 0 = a canonical chestnut whose punchline the judge could recite before reaching it, transcribed with no alteration. Judge only recognisability and staleness of the material as text; do not consider how the item might be received.

Score 10 when the text is grammatically clear, self-contained, and presents the setup and punch in an easy-to-follow form; score 0 when missing context, broken formatting, typos, or truncation obstruct comprehension.

candidates.criterion: Cleanliness of commitment to one delivery format
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the item commits, without deviation, to a single recognisable joke format: pure one-liner, question-and-answer riddle, scripted dialogue with speaker labels, narrative build, or list. 0 = no identifiable format, the text drifts or stops without a formal shape; 5 = a recognisable format that is broken somewhere, mixing narration into a riddle or adding stray commentary after the punch; 10 = one format executed strictly from first word to last, with the punch positioned exactly where that format places it and nothing appended. Score only structural conformity to a template. Do NOT judge whether the format was the right choice, whether the punch is good, or whether the item is funny; a flat joke in a perfectly clean question-and-answer shape scores 10.
candidates.upstream_parent: poster's accumulated practice in writing for this format (how many times they have done this before)

candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text contains dated public figures, events, platform conventions, current-affairs references, or period-specific slang and idiom; do not judge topicality or whether the feature or joke is good.
candidates.upstream_parent: position in the entry stream and submission timing

candidates.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate the extent of visible spelling errors, malformed grammar, inconsistent capitalization, or title-body mismatches. Judge only the textual presence of these features; do not judge whether they are good, funny, or effective.

Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of the text's bulk and elaboration, independent of content: total length, number of sentences, amount of scene-setting or narrative build before the final line, presence of dialogue turns, line breaks, paragraph breaks, embedded quotation blocks, enumerated steps or lists. 0 = a single short clause or one-liner under roughly fifteen words; 5 = two to three sentences or a short two-turn exchange; 10 = a multi-paragraph build, extended narrative, or long quoted block. Score length and structural elaboration only. Do NOT judge whether the length is earned, whether the build pays off, or whether brevity is a virtue here.

Score 0-10 for how much the text follows a conspicuous stock joke scaffold such as a question-and-answer, dialogue labels, numbered steps, or a 'what do you call/because' frame; do not judge whether the feature or joke is good.

candidates.criterion: Orthographic error as accident versus orthography as deliberate device
candidates.instruction: Score the handling of spelling and grammar. 10 = the text is clean, OR any non-standard spelling is unmistakably intentional and load-bearing, functioning as the joke's mechanism. 5 = clean but flat prose with minor slips that do not touch the joke. 0 = multiple unintentional misspellings, dropped words, or broken syntax that the joke does not use, signalling that the item was posted without a reread. Distinguish carefully: an intentional respelling that IS the punchline is a 10, not a 0.
Score 0-10 for explicit quotation, attribution, named source material, movie references, or transcription-like framing; judge sourcing signals only, not whether the joke is good or funny.
Score 10 if the punchline explicitly requires knowledge of STEM, math, grammar, or specific academic trivia to understand; score 0 if the joke requires no specialized academic knowledge.

Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the text shows signs of having been transcribed, translated, or lifted from somewhere else rather than composed for this post. Raise the score for: quoted blocks with attribution, citations, or source references; reported-speech framing that credits another teller ('I heard...', 'my friend told me', 'someone said'); dialogue rendered as a transcript with speaker labels or quotation marks; phrasing that reads as translated or non-native in its article, preposition or word-order choices; stand-up cadence or a set-up aside addressed to a live room; formatting residue such as bold or italic markers, asterisks around a title, or a stray URL or domain string. 0 = reads as written on the spot for this post, first-person and unattributed; 10 = explicitly quoted, cited, or transcribed from an external source. Score the provenance trace visible in the text only, and do NOT judge originality, plagiarism, or quality.
candidates.upstream_parent: provenance of the material (transcribed from a comedian, translated, lifted from elsewhere online) versus written for this post

candidates.criterion: Presupposed familiarity: variant, remix or knowing-repost framing
candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the text presents itself as occupying a position in a chain of already-circulating jokes rather than as newly minted: explicit repost or 'you have seen this' language, self-description as a variant or addition, sentences that assume the reader already knows the joke's form or its original, a punch that is a well-worn stock formula reused with a twist, or a structure whose payoff requires the reader to recognise a prior joke or catchphrase. 0 = presents as freshly written and self-contained, needing no prior joke; 5 = leans on a stock formula or a widely known catchphrase without acknowledging it; 10 = openly names itself as a repost, remix or reply to a joke the audience is assumed to have already seen. Score the framing and dependence on prior circulation only. Do NOT judge whether reuse is lazy or skilful, or whether the twist works.
candidates.upstream_parent: the item's position in the retelling chain of a joke that has circulated before

candidates.criterion: Reliance on Shock or Taboo Subjects
candidates.instruction: Score the extent to which the text leans on dark subject matter, sexual content, or slur-adjacent identity references. Do not judge the appropriateness or funniness.

Score the extent to which the text explicitly mentions the platform, its voting mechanisms (e.g., upvotes, front page), or its own status as a post/repost. Do not judge if this makes the text good or bad.
candidates.upstream_parent: author's practice in the format / audience engagement strategy

candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the joke's comedic content is *about* r/jokes, Reddit, posting, karma, upvotes, or the act of joke-telling itself, rather than about an external topic. 10 = the entire joke is a self-aware commentary on the subreddit/platform or its own reception as a post (e.g., mocking its own upvote prospects, describing addiction to Reddit, complaining about the sub's quality). 0 = no reference whatsoever to Reddit, subreddits, posting, karma, or the joke's own status as a post.
Score 0-10 for how much the text explicitly references the subreddit, commenters, front-page status, upvotes, or posting history; do not judge whether the feature or joke is good.
Score 0–10 for the extent of sexual, scatological, violent, religiously provocative, death-related, or slur-adjacent material; judge only taboo intensity, never whether its use is effective or funny.

Score 0-10 how much the text explicitly signals that the joke or its form has circulated before -- e.g. labeling itself a repost, apologizing for repetition, referencing a joke number/count, or presupposing the audience already knows the joke -- versus presenting itself as newly composed. 0 = no such signal, 10 = the text is primarily framed around its repost/familiarity status. Score only the presence of this framing, not whether the underlying joke is actually stale or fresh.
candidates.upstream_parent: position in the retelling chain (repost vs. original)

candidates.instruction: Score 0-10 for the amount of prose, number of setup details, line breaks, explanatory padding, and formatting bulk; do not judge whether the length improves timing or humor.
